Container.Name: messages-server
Container.Overview: Messages Server keeps your messaging accounts (Facebook Messenger, Instagram, Google Messages and Google Voice) signed in on this server, so the Messages apps on your PCs and Android phone use them from one place, at home or away through Tailscale.[br][br] [b]Setting up:[/b][br] 1. Before the first start, create the Data and Backups folders owned by user 2787 (the server's own account) with mode 700, in Unraid's terminal:[br] mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/messages-server /mnt/user/backups/messages && chown 2787:2787 /mnt/user/appdata/messages-server /mnt/user/backups/messages && chmod 700 /mnt/user/appdata/messages-server /mnt/user/backups/messages[br] 2. Start the container, then open its WebUI (https://your-server:8787/; the browser warns about the certificate once, because the server made it itself). Enter the setup code from the container's log and choose the page's password.[br] 3. The page walks you through Tailscale, your accounts, adding your phone and PCs, notifications and backups.[br][br] Your sign-ins and keys live in the Docker volume messages-server-keys, inside Docker's own storage and outside every share; the Data folder holds only what is sealed with those keys. Backups go to the Backups folder and never include a service sign-in. Set Docker's stop timeout for this container to at least 60 seconds (Auto Update Applications too), so messages being sent can finish.
Container.Requires: Create the Data and Backups folders owned by 2787:2787 with mode 700 before the first start (see the setup steps above).

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: The one port the Messages apps and the server's page use (HTTPS).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Saved sign-ins, history and paired devices, sealed with the keys volume and useless without it. Owned by 2787:2787, mode 700.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the server writes its own backups: the history and the server's identity, never a service sign-in. Owned by 2787:2787, mode 700.

Config.Name: Reach from your tailnet
Config.Description: 1 puts the server on your Tailscale network as a machine of its own, so your phone reaches it from anywhere while the port above stays on your home network. The server's page signs it in. 0 turns it off.

Config.Name: Tailscale auth key
Config.Description: Optional: a Tailscale auth key (tskey-auth-...) that signs the server in by itself the first time, instead of the page's sign-in. A tagged key lets in every device your access rules allow, not only your own. Clear it once the server is signed in.

Config.Name: Tailnet name
Config.Description: The server's name on your Tailscale network: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

Config.Name: Server names
Config.Description: Optional: the names and addresses devices reach the server by, comma-separated, written into its certificate when it is first made (devices trust its fingerprint, not these names).

Config.Name: Server page password
Config.Description: Optional: sets the page's password here instead of on its first visit (12 to 128 characters, used nowhere else). Unraid shows it in the docker command it prints.

Config.Name: Resume sign-ins at start
Config.Description: 1 resumes the accounts signed in on this server when it starts.

Config.Name: Google Messages and Voice
Config.Description: 1 runs Google Messages and Google Voice beside the server's own Google Chrome.

Config.Name: Google through Chrome
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Google is signed in by hand in the server's own Chrome, which keeps the sign-in fresh.

Config.Name: Chrome on its own display
Config.Description: Leave at 1: Chrome draws on a virtual display inside the container.

Config.Name: Network of its own
Config.Description: 1 on the bridge network: the container has a network of its own, so the page may show Google's sign-in from the server's Chrome. Set 0 with host networking.

Config.Name: Chrome without its sandbox
Config.Description: 1 runs Chrome without its own sandbox, which a container with every capability dropped cannot give it. Chrome loads only Google's sign-in pages. The project's README explains how to run with the sandbox instead.

Config.Name: Keys folder in the container
Config.Description: Leave as /keys, the volume in Extra Parameters.
